headline: Multi-omic and spatial frameworks recover disease-relevant structure from transcriptomes
label: Multi Omic Disease Signature Analysis
summary: Paired single-cell, spatial, and cfDNA datasets now let computational methods resolve disease-linked regulatory and tissue-level structure.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational recovery of disease-relevant organization from transcriptomic and multi-omic data, increasingly resolved across spatial scales and tissue geometry. multiScaleAC scores ligand-receptor interactions as a function of Gaussian kernel bandwidth within a Moran's I framework, while SFinx models spatially varying pathway activity through spatial fingerprints. CurvSeq and CurvSee couple curvature-based gland geometry to spatial transcriptomic and protein imaging data in prostate cancer. Other items infer regulatory structure: paired scRNA-seq identifies genes adapting to host liver in colorectal metastases, a pan-cancer snRNA and ATAC atlas of 60 cancer cell lines maps gene regulatory networks and a conserved EMT axis, and lncAPNet infers lncRNA-mRNA connections from patient transcriptomes. What is new is explicit scale-dependent and morphomechanical description alongside network-based inference.
